items.item_text: California Physician Assistant (PA) license.
Current PA Certification from NCCPA.
BLS/CPR certification at time of hire with commitment to get BART within 6 months of hire date.
Must be able to work various hours, days, shifts, on-call and locations based on the 24-hour Medical Center's business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Must be able to obtain UCSD Medical Staff privileges and maintain during employment.
Due to advanced practice credentialing eligibility, clinical advanced practice experience must be within the last two years.
A minimum of two (2+) years of recent high-acuity inpatient HCT or outpatient oncology Physician Assistant experience (within the last two years).
Experience in quality improvement.
Demonstrated experience in high-acuity settings, managing competing priorities with strong organizational and time management skills.
Experience working with clinical trials and the ability to identify potential clinical trial patients.

UC San Diego Health is proud to be a four-time Magnet-designated organization and has now earned Magnet with Distinction from the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC). Magnet is the gold standard for nursing excellence, achieved by only about 10% of hospitals worldwide. Magnet with Distinction is awarded to the highest-performing Magnet organizations, with only a select few earning this prestigious honor. This recognition reflects our commitment to transformational leadership, professional nursing excellence, innovation, exceptional patient outcomes, and an empowering practice environment where nurses thrive.

Under the direction of the Hematology and Cellular Therapy attending physician and APP Supervisor, the Physician Assistant (PA) provides primary medical management for oncology/HCT patients. Acts as a liaison within the HCT Program to promote consistent medical management across the health care continuum by collaborating with the multidisciplinary care team. Performs specialized procedures such as bone marrow biopsy, lumbar puncture, and skin biopsy. Presents patient cases during weekly HCT Clinical meetings. Provides patient/family and staff education. Supports the development and revision of HCT divisional policies and procedures. Participates in and/or initiates research. Participates in community outreach and networking with community physicians and other health care professionals. Provides care to HCT patients in the outpatient setting. Develops and expands role responsibilities as patient and system needs change.
While not required, a cover letter is highly recommended when applying to this position.
Must be a graduate from a physician assistant program approved by the Accreditation Review Commission on Education for the Physician Assistant (ARC-PA).
Demonstrated knowledge of stem cell transplant, CAR-T therapy, and hematologic malignancies, including treatment pathways, complications (e.g., GVHD, infection), and expected patient outcomes.
Knowledge of administration of chemotherapy and other common HCT medications.
Demonstrated understanding of oncology/HCT-specific pathophysiology, including normal and abnormal lab values and symptom management.
Strong clinical assessment skills, with the ability to recognize changes in patient condition and appropriately escalate care in a fast-paced inpatient environment.
Proven ability to work effectively within an interdisciplinary care team, collaborating with physicians, nurses, pharmacists, and ancillary staff to support coordinated patient care.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to support and educate patients and families through complex and emotionally challenging care.

Demonstrates professionalism, adaptability, emotional intelligence, and a willingness to learn, with openness to feedback and growth when caring for patients with complex oncologic and transplant-related needs.
Ability to participate in patient education, case discussions, and team-based care activities, with support and guidance from supervising providers.
